text:
Anya: Quick status from synapse-v2 embed bringup (fp16 vs per-channel int8) on wiki-recall. Summary below.

Mike: show numbers pls

Anya: run output:
fp16 recall@10: 0.812; int8 per-channel recall@10: 0.768 (-4.4%)
recall@1: fp16 0.524 vs int8 0.487 (-3.7%)
MRR: fp16 0.635 int8 0.601
avg latency (1q): fp16 23ms int8 17ms
clustering purity (kmeans k=50): fp16 0.62 int8 0.66

Sudha: that's a noticeable short-query hit?

Anya: stratified by query length: short (<5 tokens) ~8% abs drop @10, mid ~2% drop, long (>20) +0.5% gain. CSV uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/synapse-v2/1769460000/stratified.csv

Leo: did you try microbatch changes / cache?

Anya: microbatch=1 and 8 both tested; trends persist. Hypothesis: quant noise in projection head — per-channel reduces some axis noise but perturbs high-frequency short tokens.

eval-bot: Automated alert: 134k query pairs with cosine shift >0.05 between fp16 and int8. See /evals/1769460000/cosine-shift-hist.png

Mike: next steps:
- run per-tensor int6 with KL clipping quick sweep
- re-run int8 with PCA whitening on reference index
- compute NN overlap and ID-flip rates for k=1,5,10

Sudha: add bootstrap 10x subsamples (20k) for recall@10 variance

Anya: ACK; will run int6 sweep + whitening + bootstrap tomorrow AM, aim to post results EOD.

Mike: @product-team FYI — consider fp16 hot-path for <6 tokens if short-query recall degrades UX

Anya: example neighbor diffs for short queries:
- "weather": fp16 [forecast, temperature, rain] vs int8 [forecast, climate, rainfall]
- "covid": fp16 [coronavirus, pandemic, cases] vs int8 [coronavirus, vaccines, pandemic]

Leo: semantically ok but ID flips could break exact-match rerankers. Can you output top-1 cosine deltas?

Anya: will include. run metadata: torch=2.2.0, bitsandbytes=0.40, quant backend="per-channel(kl)", rng=42

Mike: thanks, looking forward to the bootstrap variance numbers :thinking_face:
